decision: Block production deployment immediately until automated red-teaming and indirect prompt injection suites (promptfoo/garak) pass.
rationale: Deploying an agent that ingests external emails without adversarial testing exposes the system to critical indirect prompt injection and data exfiltration.

decision: Reject prompt-only security and require an external input/output guardrail layer with PII/DLP filtering before release.
rationale: A system prompt is not a security boundary and can be bypassed easily via roleplay or encoding attacks.

decision: Require mandatory human-in-the-loop approval for all high blast-radius actions (DB writes and external emails).
rationale: Every model can fail under adversarial pressure; blast-radius containment requires human confirmation before irreversible mutations.

decision: Withhold security sign-off until the vendor delivers reproducible adversarial failure rates and full tool-call audit logs.
rationale: Security claims without measurable failure metrics and auditability are unverifiable.
